extracted.intended_audience: Governor and Council at Fort St. George (Madras Presidency); East India Company colonial administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and determinations for resolving outstanding territorial, revenue, and repair disputes between the Nabob of Arcot and the Rajah of Tanjore, pursuant to the treaty of 1762 and the late Act of Parliament. Guidance covers arrears (peshcush), jaghire possession (Arnee), possession of Hanamantagoody, the government share of the 1775–6 crop, and repairs/rights concerning the Anicut and Cavery banks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit extraordinary demands on the Rajah to four lacs annually
rubrics_metrics.description: We think it impolitic to insist upon any demands upon the Rajah for the expenses of the late war, beyond the sum of four lacs of pagodas annually; such a demand might tend to interrupt the harmony which should prevail between the Company and the Rajah, and impede the great objects of the general system we have already so fully explained to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not press the Rajah for more than four lacs of pagodas in respect of late-war expenses; prioritize maintaining harmony between the Company and the Rajah and the broader system already directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Nabob's just claim to arrears (peshcush) while using Company as intermediary
rubrics_metrics.description: It is by no means our intention in any manner to affect the just claim which the Nabob has on the Rajah for the arrears due to him on account of peshcush, for the regular payment of which we became guaranty by the treaty of 1762; but we have already expressed to you our hopes that the Nabob may be induced to allow these arrears and the growing payments, when due, to be received by the Company, and carried in discharge of his debt to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use every means to convince the Nabob to allow arrears and future payments to be received by the Company and applied to his debt; when the debt is discharged, exert efforts to insure the constant and regular payment of it into the Nabob's own hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring arrears to account as soon as practicable consistent with resources
rubrics_metrics.description: We are unable to decide how far this proposal may be consistent with the present state of the Rajah's resources; but we direct you to use all proper means to bring these arrears to account as soon as possible, consistently with a due attention to this consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locally assess Rajah's resources and employ appropriate measures to bring arrears to account promptly, balancing expediency with fairness to the Rajah's capacity to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confine treaty-based settlement duty to matters connected with treaty of 1762
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of the treaty of 1762 appear to be restricted to the arrears of tribute to be paid to the Nabob for his past claims, and to the quantum of the Rajah's future tribute or peshcush... the only point now in dispute, which appears to us to be so immediately connected with it as to bring it within the strict line of our duty to ascertain and settle according to the terms and stipulations of the treaty, is that respecting Arnee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding what disputes must be ascertained and settled 'according to the principles and the terms and stipulations contained in the treaty of 1762', limit that strict duty primarily to claims clearly tied to the treaty (notably Arnee); other disputes may be considered under broader political judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerate and investigate the specific outstanding points of dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: On a retrospect ... we find the following points remain unadjusted, viz. 1st, Whether the jaghire of Arnee shall be enjoyed by the Nabob, or delivered up... 2d, Whether the fort and district of Hanamantagoody... 3rd, To whom the government share of the crop of the Tanjore country, of the year 1775-6, properly belongs. Lastly, Whether the Rajah has a right... to be permitted to repair such part of the Anicut... as lie within the district of Trichinopoly...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a complete knowledge of facts and circumstances relating to each enumerated point and evaluate how far each is connected to treaty obligations; examine all available materials with circumspection before deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require satisfactory documentary/evidentiary support before complying with territorial claims (Arnee)
rubrics_metrics.description: The research has offered no evidence in support of the Rajah's claim, nor even any lights whereby we can discover in what degree of relationship... the Rajah now stands, or formerly stood, with the Killadar of Arnee... we should think ourselves highly reprehensible in complying with the Rajah's request...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not grant possession or rights (e.g., Arnee) in favor of a claimant absent satisfactory records or evidence of title/relationship; where evidence is insufficient, decline compliance or demand fuller proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore hereditary jaghire to heir unless forfeited, but suspend if peace requires
rubrics_metrics.description: We therefore direct, that, if the heir of Tremaul Row is not at present in possession of the jaghire, and has not, by any violation of the treaty, or act of disobedience, incurred a forfeiture thereof, he be forthwith restored to the possession of it; But if any powerful motive of regard to the peace and tranquillity of the Carnatic shall in your judgment render it expedient to suspend the execution of these orders, in that case you are with all convenient speed to transmit to us your proceedings thereupon, with the full state of the facts, and of the reasons which have actuated your conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restore the rightful heir immediately unless there is evidence of forfeiture; if local peace considerations counsel suspension, suspend but promptly report full facts and reasons to the Commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline to dispossess Nabob of Hanamantagoody absent convincing proof
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the fort and district of Hanamantagoody ... we must confess they fall very short of demonstrating to us the truth of that fact. And we find... the Nabob is now in the actual possession of this fort and district; and we are not warranted, by any document we have seen, to concur with the wishes of the Rajah to dispossess him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documentary evidence is inadequate and Nabob has actual possession, do not concur with Rajah's request to dispossess the Nabob.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the government share of the 1775–6 crop as belonging to the de facto sovereign (the Nabob), but avoid imposing further burdens on the Rajah
rubrics_metrics.description: We must be of opinion that the government share of the crop of 1776 belonged to the Nabob, as the then reigning sovereign of the kingdom of Tanjore, he being, de facto, in the full and absolute possession of the government thereof; and consequently that the assignments made by him of the government share of the crop were valid.... we would by no means be understood by this opinion to suggest that any further demands ought to be made upon the Rajah, in respect of such parts of the government share of the crop as were collected by his people.... we should think it highly unjust that the Rajah should be now compelled either to pay the supposed balances, whatever they may be, or be called upon to render a specific account of the collection made by his people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize Nabob's de facto right to that year's government share and the validity of his assignments; nevertheless, refrain from pressing the Rajah for further accounts or balances long after the events—exercise clemency and fairness given lapse of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcease further demands and allow local disposition of Rajah's deposit absent difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: We direct you to surcease any further demands from the Rajah on that account... as our sentiments and intentions are so fully expressed upon the whole subject, we presume you, who are upon the spot, can have no doubt or difficulty in making such an application of the deposit as will be consistent with those principles of justice whereon our sentiments are founded. But should any such difficulty suggest itself, you will suspend any application of the deposit, until you have fully explained the same to us, and have received our further orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop pursuing additional claims against the Rajah regarding the crop; apply the one-lac deposit in a manner locally consistent with justice unless difficulties arise, in which case pause and consult the Commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and prioritize repair of the Anicut and Cavery banks; refer to prior investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the repairs of the Anicut and banks of the Cavery we have upon various occasions fully expressed to you our sentiments, and in particular in our general letter of the 4th July, 1777, we referred you to the investigation and correspondence on that subject of the year 1764, and to the report made by Mr. ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the Anicut as the source of prosperity requiring considerable annual expense and frequent repairs; follow previous investigations/reports (notably 1764) in determining rights and obligations for repairs, and ensure its maintenance to prevent general injury to the country.
